title: LLM custody handoff and performance-signature pipeline
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Implement an end-to-end custody and performance-signature pipeline for community/OSS LLMs that enforces provenance checks, runs hermetic conversion in sandboxed containers, executes deterministic validation (smoke + microbench), and publishes a signed performance profile + recommended pin. The pipeline should produce a reproducible artifact: signed manifest (hashes + provenance), conversion container provenance, deterministic benchmark outputs, and an automatic pin recommendation with rollback metadata. This ticket coordinates infra (sandbox), runtime harnesses, and the profile publisher. Goal: reduce manual triage and speed safe model publication from intake to pin by 60% while preserving reproducibility and safety gates.
acceptance_criteria: Weights ingestion produces a signed manifest containing origin URL, checksum, uploader identity, and observed filesystem layout
Conversion runs inside a hermetic, ephemeral container template and emits a conversion fingerprint (container image digest + conversion args) that is recorded in the manifest
Deterministic validation suite (smoke, 16-step latency microbench, KV cache consistency) passes on the converted artifact and outputs reproducible result blobs
Performance signature (latency P50/P95, memory footprint, throughput at 128/256 token windows) is generated and signed with platform key and stored in the profile catalog
Automated pin suggestion logic emits a pin candidate with a confidence score and fallback mapping to compatible model variants
Canary rollout mechanism exercises the pinned variant on a controlled fraction of traffic and records regressions to the regression dashboard
Rollback metadata and a one-click unpin action are available in the console for the new pin
End-to-end run is logged with links to conversion container, signed manifest, validation artifacts, and performance telemetry
technical_notes: Provenance: use SHA-256 of original tarball + file-level manifest. Store uploader signature (OIDC subject) and optional GH release link if present
Conversion: standardize on containerized conversions using our convert-runtime:v2 image. Conversion args are canonicalized into a deterministic argument order and random seeds are fixed
Determinism: seed RNGs (PyTorch/CUDA/NumPy), disable non-deterministic kernels where possible, run a two-pass smoke with toggled CPU/CUDA to cross-validate
Validation: include KV cache state replay — generate a canonical prompt set and verify token-by-token logits equivalence within numeric tolerances for quantized variants
Performance signature format: JSON-LD with fields {model_id, pin, seq_window, batch_size, p50_ms, p95_ms, tokens_per_sec, mem_gb, env_meta, conversion_fingerprint}
Signing: use platform KMS to sign the profile; store public verification key in the profile catalog and expose verify endpoint
Pin logic: prefer existing pins if the new artifact matches conversion_fingerprint and performance delta < 5% across key metrics; otherwise recommend new pin with rationale
Telemetry: emit structured events for each stage (ingest, convert:start/finish, validate:pass/fail, publish:profile) for observability and SLO tracking

review_feedback: Malik Patel — 'Nice end-to-end scope. Please make sure we limit container runtime secrets and mount keys read-only; recommend ephemeral KMS tokens.'
J. Doe (Runtime) — 'Conversion args need normalization step; otherwise we get spurious pin churn. Add canonicalizer util.'
Security — 'Threat model looks OK, but add a step to validate signed manifests against known allowlist or provenance heuristics.'
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Non-deterministic conversion outputs causing pin churn. Mitigation: canonicalize args, seed RNGs, run cross-hardware validation and require repeatable fingerprint in two independent runs.
Risk: Malicious upstream payloads in community uploads. Mitigation: run conversions inside network-restricted sandboxes, attach static analysis checks, and hold for manual review on heuristic flags.
Risk: Performance regressions slipping to prod. Mitigation: gated canary rollout with automatic rollback if p50 or token-throughput delta exceeds thresholds for 30m.
Risk: Signing key compromise. Mitigation: KMS best practices + rotation policy + audit logs; include signature revocation metadata in profile catalog.
test_plan: Unit tests for manifest canonicalization and signature verification
End-to-end integration test that runs ingestion -> conversion -> validation in a fully mocked sandbox CI job
Determinism regression job: run conversion twice on 3 hardware variants and assert fingerprint equality
Canary smoke job: run 1% synthetic traffic for 60 minutes, report regression metrics to dashboard
Manual playbook: steps to unpin and fallback to previous variant in the console
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (staging): enable pipeline for curated community uploads only; validate with 10 canary runs over 1 week
Stage 2 (pilot): enable for beta customers on dedicated accounts with opt-in pins; monitor regressions and manual audit results
Stage 3 (GA): enable automated pin suggestions for all public onboards with scheduled key rotation and extended telemetry retention
Rollback: if canary failure criteria met, automatically mark pin as deprecated and route traffic to compatible fallback variant
